item.description:
### Added - **POV Start** (⌘7): a new module that runs a proof of value from one place. - **Tenant Readiness:** a read-only check of what a POV needs, each with the fix: pending ZIA changes, SSL Inspection rules above Zscaler's recommended exemptions, isolation profiles, the Zscaler Trusted Resolver, identity-provider groups, licences; ZPA's AppProtection and Privileged Remote Access, App Connectors online, a PRA portal, web certificates; Client Connector's enrolled devices; ZDX. - **Customer Intake:** the customer's name, a prefix made from it, the internal domain, VPN gateways, the products in scope and a market preset (Healthcare, Financial services, General enterprise, Education or none). One click fills every module; everything stays editable in its module. - **Build the POV**, then **Dry Run & Apply:** each product in order (Client Connector first), one dry run across them and one Apply, through each module's own checks and Undo. - **POV Tests:** a test for each policy the POV has, with the steps and what to expect, marked Pass, Fail or Skip with a note (saved as Markdown and added to the summary report); "Prove it" shows which URL Filtering rule the tenant applies to a URL; a DLP test kit of made-up patient, card, Social Security and CUI data. - **ZPA:** an access, timeout, inspection or isolation rule the wizard made gains the application segments a re-run adds (Undo puts it back). - **Bulk Rule Manager:** the ZIA tab also lists the tenant's custom DLP engines, DLP dictionaries and URL categories (the wizard's among them), so a POV can be cleaned up completely. Rules are deleted before the engines, dictionaries and categories they use.
### Changed - **ZTH Ebook:** uncategorized and miscellaneous sites open in Browser Isolation (a caution page without an isolation profile) instead of being blocked. Strict still blocks them and Permissive still shows a caution page. - **Update in place (ZIA):** a rule updated to match the plan now loses what the plan leaves out, such as an isolation profile on a rule that now blocks, or categories and apps added in the portal; who the rule applies to and fields the wizard never sets stay. Undo puts back only the fields the run changed, so a rule switched off or moved since stays that way. - **Endpoint DLP** watches the framework's own data first (PHI identifiers for HIPAA, CUI markings for NIST 800-171, and so on), and says when a rule was created without an engine. - **Rule names:** shortening a long name to ZIA's 31 characters never abbreviates the prefix. - **Advanced Threat Protection:** on a tenant whose feature flags block some of its AI settings through the API, the rest are still applied, and the ones left out are named. - A rate-limited Client Connector or ZDX dry run runs again by itself at most three times, a minute apart at least. - **Disconnect** waits while an Apply, Undo or deletion is running, and each module's results are cleared when the connection changes. - The printable summary report is one file in the temporary folder, removed when the app starts and quits.
### Fixed - **Client Connector:** re-running with the name of a ZPW- app profile that was assigned to groups or users in the portal no longer makes it apply to all users: the dry run stops instead. A forwarding profile updated in place now warns that portal changes are reset, naming the app profiles that use it. - **Client Connector:** an app profile write that got no answer is no longer rolled back (it may have gone through), and it's never sent twice; the profile is recorded for Undo when it's there. Editing Domain Inclusions no longer fails the "all domains" check after Apply. The Windows install script reads names with accents correctly. - **ZIA:** the dry run no longer says a rule's scope is left as it is when the rule will be updated; an update or setting that got no answer is recorded so Undo can check it; Apply catches an edit made in the portal after the dry run even past the first 140 characters of a field. - **ZPA:** Undo and Check for Drift refuse a run record for another ZPA customer; a read that fails during the dry run says so instead of looking like nothing in the tenant; Apply stops if a segment to update was changed after the dry run, and the dry run shows its current destinations and ports. - **Summary report:** after an Apply it lists the rules as applied, and never another connection's results. - **Bulk Rule Manager:** deletes only the ticked rules the page shows, and the confirmation names each one. - **Licences:** an answer the app can't read no longer marks every module as unlicensed. The Cloud Sandbox licence starts over with each connection, and one loaded from a selections file is kept. - **Selections files:** a whole policy type set to Isolate is ignored with a note, as the Rules page can't show it.
